english_verification.review_scope: Read representative F29 history and native English localization for the Kaxhkeddax/Kelmaxherho factions and Sunkiller Xhaz country name. Read actual Markdown chunks from three fixed-revision pages for the default 1445 outcome, the 1443 alliance context, and Sandfang history. This was not an exhaustive event or mission audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The official 2025 development diary counted 57 missions; the current local mission file has 58 direct definitions. The English article preserves both with their version boundary.
The source lists a second gnoll polity as a similar country, but its current English name was not established in this representative check and is explicitly left unresolved in that comparison field.
Wiki 1445 death and dissolution are the default setting outcome after the start, not a guaranteed player-campaign result; all faction outcomes and runtime reachability were not audited.

rationale.campaign_length: 58 direct missions in the current files, from the wars in Bulwar to devouring the Moon and Sun.
rationale.colonization: The late game reaches distant regions, but its central arc is conquest rather than colonial development.
rationale.complexity: War tempo, manpower, Demonic Power, religious interactions, estate favor, and intercontinental missions must be managed together.
rationale.dark_story: Enslavement, sacrifice, devouring rulers, and world destruction are gameplay objectives, not mere background.
rationale.difficulty: A correct loop can snowball rapidly, but the opening war, poor resource choices, and late intercontinental management punish mistakes.
rationale.diplomacy: Subjects and tributaries can ease administration, but alliances ultimately serve betrayal, annexation, and sacrifice.
rationale.early_pressure: The decisive war with Jaddar begins almost immediately; losing ends the F29 route.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Military sorcery, demonic rites, Hellgates, devoured gods, and the attempt to kill the Sun define the campaign.
rationale.narrative_density: The opening rivalry, two estates, demonic apotheosis, and cosmic finale form one continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: Domestic development mainly supports conquest and mission requirements; there is no independent peaceful-building route.
rationale.trade_economy: Money mainly comes from raiding, reparations, and coastal attacks; trade is not the country's central fantasy.
rationale.warfare: War is the absolute core loop, from the opening showdown to intercontinental sacrifice.

identity.appearance: A playable Sandfang Gnoll country at the 1444 start, entering a decisive war with the Jaddari Legion almost immediately.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
For Zokka, new to leadership of a Far Salahad gnoll pack, it was just another day hunting in the harsh desert heat. An insufficiently guarded caravan, demonically-enhanced strength, a brutal ambush; the story writes itself. His pack ate well that night, dining on their slaughtered foes. A strong success for the new pack-leader, but nothing more notable than that.

For the elves of Sareyand, who awaited a caravan that never arrived, and found little but sun-scorched bones when they looked for it — it was horror. A whisper of an age long past, an age thought banished forevermore by Surael's incarnation Jaher. For those Sun Elves Zokka had made a meal of were the first elves to be devoured by gnolls in centuries. A force was mustered to confront the gnoll. It came back battered, scorched by demonflame. The next simply vanished into the sands. Even the Desert Legion could not hunt him down. And all the while, in the Salahad, the legend of Zokka, Devourer-of-Suns, grew and grew.

description.text: Out of the arid Salahad, various peoples make coin in various ways. The Desert Legion pursues the staid job of caravan-guards, the Mašnsih tend their flocks, merchants of east and west grow rich selling to the other side. But the gnolls of Zokka know the best way. Just loot everyone else's! Ever since that first caravan, Zokka's horde has plundered everything that can be taken, and destroyed what cannot be, after laying their foes to waste.

description.text:
Bulwari children fear Zokka's gnashing teeth. Sareyandi soldiers fear his demonic strength. But the cleverest scholars and most studied generals of the Desert Legion? They fear what truly makes him dangerous, his cunning nature.
That trait was on full display when he arranged a meeting with the Matriarch Astárta Siadunó in 1424 AA. They both had dreams of a new 'Age of Monsters'; he sought to resurrect gnollish Bulwar, she hoped to return the harpy matriarchy of Siadanlén to predominance in the Far Salahad. And they both knew those dreams would require the slaughter of Sun Elves, and any else who would stand before them. With the mixing of a drop of harpy and gnollish blood into a bottle of wine, then quaffed by the two rulers, the pact was sealed — and Surael himself must have shivered.

description.text:
Zokka's pack began small, but grew as more and more gnolls heard of his legend and sought to join him. Even after he had consolidated much of the Far Salahad, Zokka knew the value of a constant stream of fresh blood.

When the packs of Kogzalla and Koggraffa to the south swore their loyalty to him, Zokka didn't seek to claim their lands directly, knowing this would put him in conflict with the larger packs of Sarhal. Instead he demanded they send a regular tithe of soldiers and supplies to ensure that his pack were able to replenish any losses to battle or famine swiftly.

description.text:
Zokka prizes loyalty — to him — above much else, and as such, his court is dominated by those gnolls who have been with them ever since those early days. Their position is entrenched, unassailable, and they know it. They make sure every new member to the court, behind in clout compared to their fellow comrades, know this too, by harassing and bullying them endlessly.

This makes it incredibly rare for a new gnoll to rise up in status, rarely happening except in the case of a particularly demon-touched individual. As an unintended consequence, it also prevents potential spies who would rather go home with no information than stand another day of torment.

description.text:
It is said that Zokka came to command his pack by summoning a demon that swallowed the commanding gnoll whole. It is said that in the Salahad's darkest nights, you can still hear her screams drifting on the wind, as that demon tortures her forevermore.
Whatever that rumor's truth, it is certain that few if any gnollish tribes are as zealous as Zokka's in consorting with demons to gain unnatural power. From minor rituals at nightfall and dawn, to pre-battle rites, to post-battle sacrifices, the Xhazobkult infuses every piece of life in Zokka's pack.

description.text:
The strong rule. The weak serve. Power is all that matters.

This philosophy once dominated Bulwar, but the gnolls of Zokka now see the land covered in weak kingdoms that would rather pray to living failures than embrace that truth. No matter. Every gnoll in the pack knows it, is united by it, and will show the weak just what that belief entails. If that takes drowning the land in blood and hellfire, so be it.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid if you want peaceful development, stable diplomacy, low-intensity play, or do not want themes of enslavement, sacrifice, and world destruction.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Concentrate your forces to defeat Jaddar, then sustain continuous wars with razing, mercenaries, demonic rites, and devoured rulers while managing the two estates and gathering gods and sacrifices across continents.
player_overview.overview: Zokka is a Sandfang Gnoll warlord in 1444, and his first priority is winning a decisive war against Jaddar. Afterward, sustain continuous conquest through razing, Demonic Power, and devouring enemy rulers, while balancing favor between the Kaxhkeddax and Kelmaxherho estates. The campaign ultimately tears open Hell, devours the Moon, and challenges the Sun. The cost is that there is almost no time for peace.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy an extreme villain narrative, a very long mission tree, continuous expansion, magical catastrophe, and an absurd cosmic finale.
signature_features: The opening battle between Zokka and Jaddar decides which imperial route can continue.
A special peace treaty lets Zokka devour an enemy ruler and force the defeated country to release nations and subjects.
Balance favor between the Kaxhkeddax and Kelmaxherho before escalating continental conquest into a global catastrophe that devours the Moon and challenges the Sun.
player_overview.tagline: Become Zokka the Sun-Eater, feeding a true rite to kill the Sun with the world's wars, souls, and gods.

reasons: Zokka and Jaddar mirror one another; the opening outcome immediately rewrites Bulwari history.
Devouring rulers and managing favor between two dedicated estates make the playstyle unmistakable.
The story escalates from regional conquest to an invasion of Hell, devouring the Moon, and challenging the Sun.
Extremely high expansion potential suits experienced players who enjoy creating a snowball.
similar_countries: Gnollakaz / [second source-listed gnoll polity; English name unresolved]
warnings: Losing the opening duel ends Zokka's route and switches the player to Tluukt.
The resource loop is unintuitive; manpower, money, monarch points, and Demonic Power can all run low together.
Intercontinental wars, coring, rebellions, and long mission requirements can cause late-game fatigue.
The offline Wiki adds the Sandfang pack's background, its alliance with Tluukt, and the 1445 default setting outcome; that outcome is not inevitable in a player campaign.

values.rationale: Enslavement, sacrifice, devouring enemy rulers, and destructive demonic objectives run through the main campaign and directly harm nearly every values dimension.
red_flags: A goal of destroying the world.
